records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶל־בָּנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ וְאַגִּ֣ידָה לָכֶ֔ם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־יִקְרָ֥א אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And called Jacob to his sons and said, gather yourselves, that I may tell you what will befall you in [the] end of the days.
pieces: Jacob summoned his sons and said, "Come together, and I will tell you what lies ahead for you in the time to come."

L.1: And Jacob called his sons and said, "Gather yourselves together, so that I may tell you what will happen to you in the end of the days."

R.1: Jacob sent for his sons and said, "Come near, and I will tell you what is going to happen to you in the years ahead."

decisions.choice: the end of the days: the time to come
alternatives: the last days of the world
decisions.reason: The phrase looks ahead to a later time, here the days when the sons have become tribes in the land. The prophets use the same words for the time when God brings his purposes to their goal (Isaiah 2:2; Hosea 3:5).

decisions.choice: a father's last words
decisions.reason: As Isaac had done (27:1-4), the dying head of the family speaks words over his sons that shape their future.

decisions.choice: in the end of the days
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase; Balanced and Readable say what it means here (meaning decision m1).

records.source: הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֲבִיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Assemble and hear, sons of Jacob, and listen to Israel your father.
pieces: "Come together and hear, you sons of Jacob; give ear to Israel your father.

L.2: "Assemble and hear, sons of Jacob; and listen to Israel your father.

R.2: "Sons of Jacob, gather together and hear me. Pay attention to your father Israel.

decisions.choice: Jacob's blessings are poetry
decisions.reason: From here to verse 27 Jacob speaks in poetry, in pairs of lines where the second says the first again in other words: "sons of Jacob" and "Israel your father". Several sayings play on the meaning of a son's name. Many lines are rare or hard words, so a number of readings are uncertain.

decisions.choice: Jacob ... Israel: one man, two names
decisions.reason: The parallel lines use both of the patriarch's names (32:28); his sons will become the tribes of Israel.

records.source: רְאוּבֵן֙ בְּכֹ֣רִי אַ֔תָּה כֹּחִ֖י וְרֵאשִׁ֣ית אוֹנִ֑י יֶ֥תֶר שְׂאֵ֖ת וְיֶ֥תֶר עָֽז׃
records.gloss: Reuben, my firstborn [are] you, my strength and [the] first of my vigor, excess of dignity and excess of power.
pieces: Reuben, my firstborn, you are my strength, the first child of my vigor, standing above the rest in honor, above the rest in power.

L.3: Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength and the first of my vigor, preeminent in dignity and preeminent in power.

R.3: Reuben, you are my oldest son. You were born when I was young and strong. As my firstborn you had the first place in honor and in power.

decisions.choice: the first of my vigor: the first child of his father's strength
decisions.reason: The same words describe the firstborn's right to a double share in Deuteronomy 21:17. Reuben was born first, to Leah (29:32).

decisions.choice: preeminent: having more than the rest
decisions.reason: Yeter means what is over and above. The next verse turns the same root against him: "you will not excel".

decisions.choice: You were born when I was young and strong
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase in plain words.

records.source: פַּ֤חַז כַּמַּ֨יִם֙ אַל־תּוֹתַ֔ר כִּ֥י עָלִ֖יתָ מִשְׁכְּבֵ֣י אָבִ֑יךָ אָ֥ז חִלַּ֖לְתָּ יְצוּעִ֥י עָלָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: Reckless as water, not you will excel, for you went up [to the] beds of your father; then you defiled [it]; my couch he went up.
pieces: Wild as surging water, you will not hold first place, for you mounted your father's bed. Then you defiled it: he climbed onto my couch!

L.4: Reckless as water, you will not excel, for you went up to your father's bed; then you defiled [it]: he went up to my couch!

R.4: But you are like a flood that no one can hold back, so the first place will not be yours. You got into your father's bed and slept with his wife. You brought shame on my bed!

decisions.choice: reckless as water: uncontrolled, boiling over
decisions.reason: Pachaz describes reckless, undisciplined people (Judges 9:4; Zephaniah 3:4). Like water that bursts its banks, Reuben could not hold himself back.

decisions.choice: you went up to your father's bed
decisions.reason: Reuben slept with Bilhah, his father's concubine (35:22). Jacob said nothing then; now he speaks. Because of it Reuben lost the rights of the firstborn (1 Chronicles 5:1).

decisions.choice: he went up: Jacob turns from Reuben
decisions.reason: The last line changes from "you" to "he", as if Jacob turns away from his son to speak of the deed to the others.

decisions.choice: slept with his wife
alternatives: went up to your father's bed
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the euphemism means. Bilhah was Jacob's concubine, a slave woman given to him as a wife (30:4).

records.source: שִׁמְע֥וֹן וְלֵוִ֖י אַחִ֑ים כְּלֵ֥י חָמָ֖ס מְכֵרֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Simeon and Levi [are] brothers; weapons of violence [are] their swords.
pieces: Simeon and Levi are brothers indeed; violence is what their blades are made for.

L.5: Simeon and Levi are brothers; their swords are weapons of violence.

R.5: Simeon and Levi are just alike. They use their swords for violence.

decisions.choice: brothers: alike in character
decisions.reason: They were full brothers, sons of Leah, but the word here means more: they acted together, as at Shechem (34:25).

decisions.choice: their swords
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. "Swords" fits the parallel with "weapons"; others connect it with words for planning or for trading.

decisions.choice: violence: chamas
decisions.reason: The same word named the evil that filled the earth before the flood (6:11).

decisions.choice: brothers indeed
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "indeed" to carry the sense of meaning decision m1; Readable says "just alike".

records.source: בְּסֹדָם֙ אַל־תָּבֹ֣א נַפְשִׁ֔י בִּקְהָלָ֖ם אַל־תֵּחַ֣ד כְּבֹדִ֑י כִּ֤י בְאַפָּם֙ הָ֣רְגוּ אִ֔ישׁ וּבִרְצֹנָ֖ם עִקְּרוּ־שֽׁוֹר׃
records.gloss: Into their council not let come my soul; with their assembly not let be united my honor; for in their anger they killed a man, and in their will they hamstrung an ox.
pieces: May I never take part in their secret plans, and may my honor stay far from their gatherings. In their rage they murdered men, and for their own pleasure they lamed oxen.

L.6: Into their council let my soul not come; with their assembly let my honor not be joined; for in their anger they killed men, and in their self-will they hamstrung oxen.

R.6: I want no part in their plans. I will not join their group. They got angry and killed men. They cut the legs of oxen just because they felt like it.

decisions.choice: my soul ... my honor: my whole self
decisions.reason: The two nouns are parallel: Jacob's life and his dignity. Kavod, honor, is also read by some with other vowels as kaved, "liver", the seat of feeling, which gives a similar sense.

decisions.choice: a man ... an ox: collective singulars
decisions.reason: Hebrew poetry often uses a singular for a whole group. At Shechem the brothers killed every male of the town (34:25-26).

decisions.choice: hamstrung oxen: cut their leg tendons
decisions.reason: To hamstring is to cut the tendons behind the knee, crippling the animal (Joshua 11:6). Chapter 34 says they took the livestock; this line adds senseless cruelty. With other vowels the last word could be "wall".

decisions.choice: men, oxen
decisions.reason: English plurals carry the collective sense (meaning decision m2).

records.source: אָר֤וּר אַפָּם֙ כִּ֣י עָ֔ז וְעֶבְרָתָ֖ם כִּ֣י קָשָׁ֑תָה אֲחַלְּקֵ֣ם בְּיַעֲקֹ֔ב וַאֲפִיצֵ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: Cursed [be] their anger, for [it is] fierce, and their fury, for it is hard; I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
pieces: Their anger is fierce and their rage is merciless; may both be cursed! I will break them apart among Jacob and spread them out across Israel.

L.7: Cursed be their anger, for it is fierce, and their wrath, for it is cruel! I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.

R.7: May their fierce anger be cursed, and their cruel rage! I will split them up and scatter them among the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: cursed be their anger: the deed, not the men
decisions.reason: Jacob curses their anger, not his sons themselves.

decisions.choice: divided and scattered
decisions.reason: Simeon received towns inside Judah's land rather than a territory of its own (Joshua 19:1-9). Levi received no land but towns spread through all the tribes (Joshua 21). Later Levi's scattering became an honor, when the Levites took their stand on God's side and were set apart for his service (Exodus 32:26-29; Deuteronomy 33:8-11).

decisions.choice: Jacob ... Israel: the people
decisions.reason: Here the two names mean the nation descended from Jacob.

records.source: יְהוּדָ֗ה אַתָּה֙ יוֹד֣וּךָ אַחֶ֔יךָ יָדְךָ֖ בְּעֹ֣רֶף אֹיְבֶ֑יךָ יִשְׁתַּחֲוּ֥וּלְךָ֖ בְּנֵ֥י אָבִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Judah, you, will praise you your brothers; your hand [will be] on [the] neck of your enemies; will bow down to you [the] sons of your father.
pieces: Judah, you are the one your brothers will praise. Your hand will grip your enemies by the neck; the sons of your father will bow low before you.

L.8: Judah, you, your brothers will praise you; your hand will be on the neck of your enemies; the sons of your father will bow down to you.

R.8: Judah, your brothers will honor you with praise. You will defeat your enemies. All your father's other sons will bow low in front of you.

decisions.choice: Judah ... will praise you: a play on his name
decisions.reason: Yehudah sounds like yoducha, "they will praise you". Leah named him with the same verb: "This time I will praise the LORD" (29:35).

decisions.choice: your hand on the neck of your enemies: victory
decisions.reason: The picture is of seizing a fleeing enemy from behind.

decisions.choice: your father's sons will bow down to you
decisions.reason: Isaac had blessed Jacob with these words (27:29). Joseph's brothers bowed before him in Egypt, but the lasting rule goes to Judah, the tribe of David's kings (1 Chronicles 5:2).

decisions.choice: You will defeat your enemies
alternatives: your hand will be on the neck of your enemies
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture.

records.source: גּ֤וּר אַרְיֵה֙ יְהוּדָ֔ה מִטֶּ֖רֶף בְּנִ֣י עָלִ֑יתָ כָּרַ֨ע רָבַ֧ץ כְּאַרְיֵ֛ה וּכְלָבִ֖יא מִ֥י יְקִימֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: A cub of a lion [is] Judah; from [the] prey, my son, you have gone up. He crouches, he lies down like a lion, and like a lioness; who will rouse him?
pieces: Judah is a young lion; my son, you have come up from the kill. He crouches and stretches out like a lion, like a lioness: who would risk waking him?

L.9: Judah is a lion's cub; from the prey, my son, you have gone up. He crouches, he lies down like a lion, and like a lioness; who will rouse him?

R.9: My son Judah, you are like a lion cub coming home from the hunt. He lies stretched out like a lion, like a lioness. No one would dare to wake him!

decisions.choice: Judah the lion
decisions.reason: The lion became Judah's emblem. Balaam uses these words of all Israel (Numbers 24:9), and Revelation 5:5 calls Christ "the Lion of the tribe of Judah".

decisions.choice: you have gone up from the prey: returned from the kill
alternatives: you have grown up on prey
decisions.reason: The lion goes up from the hunt to its den, fed and strong, and lies down in safety.

decisions.choice: lioness: a second word for lion
decisions.reason: Lavi is a poetic word for a lion, often taken as a lioness. The two words make the usual pair of parallel lines.

decisions.choice: No one would dare to wake him!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question, which expects the answer "no one", into a statement.

records.source: לֹֽא־יָס֥וּר שֵׁ֨בֶט֙ מִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וּמְחֹקֵ֖ק מִבֵּ֣ין רַגְלָ֑יו עַ֚ד כִּֽי־יָבֹ֣א שִׁיל֔וֹ וְל֖וֹ יִקְּהַ֥ת עַמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Not will depart [the] scepter from Judah, nor [the] ruler's staff from between his feet, until that comes shiloh, and to him [will be the] obedience of [the] peoples.
pieces: The scepter will not pass from Judah, nor the staff of command from between his feet, until its rightful owner comes; the peoples will obey him.

L.10: The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he comes to whom it [belongs], and to him [will be] the obedience of the peoples.

R.10: The right to rule will not be taken from Judah. A ruler's staff will stay in his family until the one it truly belongs to comes. The peoples of the world will obey him.

decisions.choice: until he comes to whom it belongs
decisions.reason: This is one of the hardest lines in Genesis. The word shiloh can be read as "the one to whom it belongs". Ezekiel 21:27 seems to echo the line that way: "until he comes whose right it is". The early translations into Greek, Syriac and Aramaic took it along these lines, and Jewish and Christian interpreters read it of a coming king. Others take Shiloh as a name or title of that king, or divide the letters as "tribute to him", or read the town of Shiloh, where the tabernacle later stood (Joshua 18:1). Every reading looks to a ruler from Judah to whom the nations submit.

decisions.choice: the spelling of shiloh
decisions.reason: The Masoretic text notes in its margin a slightly different spelling of this word. The difference is one of spelling only and does not change the reading.

decisions.choice: scepter and staff: the signs of a ruler
decisions.reason: A king held his staff of office upright between his feet as he sat on his throne. The promise was kept in David's line (2 Samuel 7:16).

decisions.choice: the obedience of the peoples
decisions.reason: Yiqqahat is a rare word for obedience (Proverbs 30:17). "Peoples" reaches beyond Israel: the coming ruler will reign over nations. Christians read the verse of Jesus, the son of David (Revelation 5:5).

decisions.choice: its rightful owner / the one it truly belongs to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the reading chosen in meaning decision m1 in plain words.

records.source: אֹסְרִ֤י לַגֶּ֨פֶן֙ עִיר֔וֹ וְלַשֹּׂרֵקָ֖ה בְּנִ֣י אֲתֹנ֑וֹ כִּבֵּ֤ס בַּיַּ֨יִן֙ לְבֻשׁ֔וֹ וּבְדַם־עֲנָבִ֖ים סוּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Binding to the vine his donkey, and to the choice vine [the] son of his she-donkey, he washes in wine his garment, and in [the] blood of grapes his robe.
pieces: He will tie his donkey to the vine, the colt of his donkey to the best of the vines; he will launder his clothes in wine, his robe in the blood of grapes.

L.11: Binding his donkey to the vine, and his donkey's colt to the choice vine, he washes his garment in wine, and his robe in the blood of grapes.

R.11: There will be so many grapevines that he will tie his donkey to one, even to the best vine. There will be so much wine that he could wash his clothes in it, his robe in the red juice of grapes.

decisions.choice: tied to the vine: a land overflowing with plenty
decisions.reason: No one would tie a donkey to a precious vine where it could eat the grapes, unless vines were everywhere. Wine is as plentiful as washing water.

decisions.choice: the donkey's colt
decisions.reason: Zechariah 9:9 pictures the coming king riding on a donkey's colt, and the Gospels see that fulfilled in Jesus (Matthew 21:5).

decisions.choice: the blood of grapes: red wine
decisions.reason: The same picture of red-stained robes returns in Isaiah 63:1-3.

decisions.choice: There will be so many grapevines ... so much wine
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the pictures mean (meaning decision m1).

records.source: חַכְלִילִ֥י עֵינַ֖יִם מִיָּ֑יִן וּלְבֶן־שִׁנַּ֖יִם מֵחָלָֽב׃פ
records.gloss: Dark of eyes from wine, and white of teeth from milk.
pieces: His eyes will be dark with wine, his teeth white with milk.

L.12: His eyes [are] dark from wine, and his teeth white from milk.

R.12: His eyes will be dark from all the wine he drinks, and his teeth white from all the milk.

decisions.choice: from wine, from milk: because of plenty
alternatives: darker than wine, whiter than milk
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "from" can give a cause or a comparison. Read as cause, the line continues the picture of plenty; read as comparison, it praises Judah's looks.

decisions.choice: dark: dulled or darkened
decisions.reason: The word is rare; a related noun describes the eyes of a drunkard in Proverbs 23:29.

records.source: זְבוּלֻ֕ן לְח֥וֹף יַמִּ֖ים יִשְׁכֹּ֑ן וְהוּא֙ לְח֣וֹף אֳנִיּ֔וֹת וְיַרְכָת֖וֹ עַל־צִידֹֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Zebulun at [the] shore of [the] seas will dwell, and he [will be] a shore of ships, and his flank [will be] toward Sidon.
pieces: Zebulun will make his home where the sea meets the land; he will be a landing place for ships, his territory stretching toward Sidon.

L.13: Zebulun will dwell at the shore of the seas, and he [will be] a haven for ships, and his flank [will be] toward Sidon.

R.13: Zebulun's people will live near the sea. Ships will come to their shore. Their land will reach toward the city of Sidon.

decisions.choice: Zebulun by the sea
decisions.reason: Zebulun's land (Joshua 19:10-16) lay in Galilee, between the Sea of Galilee and the coast. The saying may mean access to the sea and its trade (Deuteronomy 33:18-19).

decisions.choice: Sidon: Phoenicia
decisions.reason: Sidon was the great Phoenician port to the north; its name stands for the whole coast (10:15, 19).

decisions.choice: Zebulun's people
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the son stands for his tribe, as in all these sayings.

records.source: יִשָּׂשכָ֖ר חֲמֹ֣ר גָּ֑רֶם רֹבֵ֖ץ בֵּ֥ין הַֽמִּשְׁפְּתָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Issachar [is] a donkey of bone, lying down between the sheepfolds.
pieces: Issachar is a strong-boned donkey, stretched out between the sheepfolds.

L.14: Issachar is a donkey of [strong] bone, lying down between the sheepfolds.

R.14: Issachar is like a powerful donkey. He lies down to rest between the sheep pens.

decisions.choice: a donkey of bone: a strong, sturdy animal
decisions.reason: Strong bones mean strength for heavy loads.

decisions.choice: between the sheepfolds
decisions.reason: The word is found only in poetry (Judges 5:16, where it means sheepfolds). Some take it as the two packs a donkey carries; either way the donkey is lying down at rest.

records.source: וַיַּ֤רְא מְנֻחָה֙ כִּ֣י ט֔וֹב וְאֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ כִּ֣י נָעֵ֑מָה וַיֵּ֤ט שִׁכְמוֹ֙ לִסְבֹּ֔ל וַיְהִ֖י לְמַס־עֹבֵֽד׃ס
records.gloss: And he saw a resting place, that [it was] good, and the land, that it [was] pleasant; and he bent his shoulder to bear, and became [a] forced laborer serving.
pieces: He found that rest was good and the land delightful, so he stooped to carry loads and was put to forced labor.

L.15: And he saw that a resting place was good, and that the land was pleasant; and he bent his shoulder to bear [burdens], and became a slave at forced labor.

R.15: He saw that resting was good and that his land was pleasant. So he let others put heavy loads on his back, and he became a servant who was forced to work for others.

decisions.choice: he saw ... he became: the future told as past
decisions.reason: The prophecy speaks of what will happen as though it were already done.

decisions.choice: forced labor: a conscripted work gang
decisions.reason: Mas oved is the forced labor that conquered peoples did for their rulers (Joshua 16:10; 1 Kings 9:21). Issachar would trade its freedom for an easy life in a good land.

decisions.choice: bearing loads: a play on Issachar's name
decisions.reason: Leah named him for a "wage" or hire, sakar (30:18); the son of hire will work for hire.

decisions.choice: slave at forced labor
decisions.reason: The work is forced, so Literal says "slave"; Balanced says "put to forced labor" and Readable "a servant who was forced to work for others", following the style guide.

records.source: דָּ֖ן יָדִ֣ין עַמּ֑וֹ כְּאַחַ֖ד שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Dan will judge his people as one of [the] tribes of Israel.
pieces: Dan will win justice for his people, a tribe of Israel like the rest.

L.16: Dan will judge his people as one of the tribes of Israel.

R.16: Dan will make sure his people are treated fairly. He will be a tribe of Israel just like the others.

decisions.choice: Dan will judge: a play on his name
decisions.reason: Dan sounds like yadin, "he will judge". Rachel named him with the same word: "God has judged me" (30:6).

decisions.choice: as one of the tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: Dan was the son of Bilhah, Rachel's slave woman, yet his tribe stands equal with the others. Samson, of the tribe of Dan, judged Israel (Judges 13:2; 15:20).

records.source: יְהִי־דָן֙ נָחָ֣שׁ עֲלֵי־דֶ֔רֶךְ שְׁפִיפֹ֖ן עֲלֵי־אֹ֑רַח הַנֹּשֵׁךְ֙ עִקְּבֵי־ס֔וּס וַיִּפֹּ֥ל רֹכְב֖וֹ אָחֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: May be Dan a serpent on [the] road, a viper on [the] path, that bites [the] heels of [the] horse, and fell its rider backward.
pieces: May Dan be a snake on the road, a horned viper beside the path, that strikes at a horse's heels and throws its rider off backward.

L.17: May Dan be a serpent on the road, a viper on the path, that bites the horse's heels so that its rider falls backward.

R.17: I pray that Dan will be like a snake lying on the road, a deadly snake on the path. It strikes a horse's heel, and the rider falls off backward.

decisions.choice: may Dan be: a wish
decisions.reason: The verb form can express a wish or simply the future.

decisions.choice: viper: a horned snake
decisions.reason: Shefifon is found only here; it is probably the horned viper that lies hidden in desert sand.

decisions.choice: the small striking the strong
decisions.reason: A small snake can bring down a horse and rider. Dan was a small tribe that won by surprise (Judges 18:27).

records.source: לִֽישׁוּעָתְךָ֖ קִוִּ֥יתִי יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: For your salvation I wait, O LORD.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation I wait in hope, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.18: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, I am waiting for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to save us.

decisions.choice: a prayer in the middle of the blessings
decisions.reason: Jacob breaks off to call on the LORD. Perhaps the picture of Dan's danger, or the troubles ahead for all his sons, moves him to pray. This is the first time the Bible uses the word yeshuah, salvation, and the only time the divine name occurs in Jacob's blessings.

decisions.choice: I wait: wait in hope
decisions.reason: Qiwwah is to wait with expectation, to hope (Psalm 25:5; Isaiah 40:31).

decisions.choice: for you to save us
decisions.reason: Readable turns the noun into a verb and supplies "us", the family Jacob is praying for.

records.source: גָּ֖ד גְּד֣וּד יְגוּדֶ֑נּוּ וְה֖וּא יָגֻ֥ד עָקֵֽב׃ס
records.gloss: Gad, a raiding band will raid him, and he will raid [at their] heel.
pieces: Gad: a raiding band will press him hard, but he will turn and press at their heels.

L.19: Gad, raiders will raid him, but he will raid at [their] heels.

R.19: Raiders will attack Gad, but he will chase them and attack them from behind.

decisions.choice: a play on Gad's name
decisions.reason: Four words in a row sound alike: gad, gedud ("raiding band"), yegudennu ("will raid him"), yagud ("he will raid"). Gad's land east of the Jordan lay open to raiders from the desert (1 Chronicles 5:18-22).

decisions.choice: at their heels
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "heel" with no "their". The letter that begins the next verse ("from Asher") may belong at the end of this one, giving "their heels"; see verse 20. The sense is the same: Gad strikes back at the raiders as they flee.

records.source: מֵאָשֵׁ֖ר שְׁמֵנָ֣ה לַחְמ֑וֹ וְה֥וּא יִתֵּ֖ן מַֽעֲדַנֵּי־מֶֽלֶךְ׃ס
records.gloss: From Asher, rich [will be] his bread, and he will provide delicacies of a king.
pieces: Out of Asher will come rich food; he will furnish fine fare for a king.

L.20: Out of Asher, his bread [will be] rich, and he will provide a king's delicacies.

R.20: Asher's land will grow the best food. He will provide fine food for kings.

decisions.choice: out of Asher
alternatives: Asher, his bread will be rich
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with the letter mem, "from". The Greek, Syriac and Latin translations read that letter with the last word of verse 19 ("their heels") and begin this verse simply "Asher". The meaning of the saying is the same; the Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Asher: happy, blessed
decisions.reason: Leah named him from a word for "happy" (30:13). His tribe settled on the fertile coast of Galilee, rich in olive oil (Deuteronomy 33:24).

decisions.choice: delicacies of a king: food fit for royal tables
decisions.reason: Asher's produce would be fine enough for kings, perhaps sold to the kings of Phoenicia nearby.

records.source: נַפְתָּלִ֖י אַיָּלָ֣ה שְׁלֻחָ֑ה הַנֹּתֵ֖ן אִמְרֵי־שָֽׁפֶר׃ס
records.gloss: Naphtali [is] a doe let loose, which gives words of beauty.
pieces: Naphtali is a deer running free that speaks lovely words.

L.21: Naphtali is a doe let loose, which gives words of beauty.

R.21: Naphtali is like a deer running free. He speaks beautiful words.

decisions.choice: a doe let loose: swift and free
decisions.reason: A deer free in open country is a picture of speed and sure footing (2 Samuel 22:34).

decisions.choice: gives words of beauty
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "words of beauty". With other vowels the same letters can mean "lambs" or young ones, and the line would say that the doe bears beautiful fawns, which suits the picture. The text as read is followed here.

records.source: בֵּ֤ן פֹּרָת֙ יוֹסֵ֔ף בֵּ֥ן פֹּרָ֖ת עֲלֵי־עָ֑יִן בָּנ֕וֹת צָעֲדָ֖ה עֲלֵי־שֽׁוּר׃
records.gloss: A son of a fruitful [one is] Joseph, a son of a fruitful [one] by a spring; daughters climb over [a] wall.
pieces: Joseph is a fruit-bearing branch, a fruit-bearing branch beside a spring, its shoots spilling over the wall.

L.22: Joseph [is] a son of a fruitful [vine], a son of a fruitful [vine] by a spring; [its] daughters climb over [the] wall.

R.22: Joseph is like a branch of a vine full of fruit, growing beside a spring. Its branches grow up and over the wall.

decisions.choice: a fruitful branch
alternatives: a young wild donkey, a wild colt by a spring, wild donkeys on the hillside
decisions.reason: This is a famous hard line. Porat is most simply "fruitful", and "son of" can mean a branch or shoot of a plant, so Joseph is a vine planted by water whose shoots, "daughters", spread over the wall (Psalm 1:3; Ezekiel 19:10). Others connect porat with pere, "wild donkey", so that the saying, like those for Issachar and Naphtali, would picture an animal: a young wild donkey by a spring. The grammar of the line is unusual either way.

decisions.choice: fruitful: an echo of Ephraim
decisions.reason: Joseph named his son Ephraim because "God has made me fruitful" (41:52); the same root sounds here.

decisions.choice: daughters: branches
decisions.reason: The shoots of the vine are called its daughters, as towns around a city are its daughters (Numbers 21:25).

decisions.choice: a son of a fruitful [vine]
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "son" and supplies the plant; Balanced and Readable say "branch", against the familiar "bough".

records.source: וַֽיְמָרֲרֻ֖הוּ וָרֹ֑בּוּ וַֽיִּשְׂטְמֻ֖הוּ בַּעֲלֵ֥י חִצִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And they made bitter [for] him and shot, and they bore a grudge [against] him, masters of arrows.
pieces: Archers made his life bitter; they shot at him and hounded him with hatred.

L.23: And they made it bitter for him and shot [at him], and they bore a grudge against him, the masters of arrows.

R.23: Enemies with bows and arrows attacked him. They shot at him and hated him.

decisions.choice: masters of arrows: archers
decisions.reason: A "master" (baal) of something is one who has it or is skilled in it.

decisions.choice: bore a grudge: the hatred Joseph suffered
decisions.reason: The verb satam is used of Esau's grudge against Jacob (27:41) and of the brothers' fear that Joseph would hold one against them (50:15). The archers picture all who attacked Joseph: his brothers, Potiphar's wife, the prison.

decisions.choice: Archers / Enemies with bows and arrows
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the subject first, where English expects it.

records.source: וַתֵּ֤שֶׁב בְּאֵיתָן֙ קַשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיָּפֹ֖זּוּ זְרֹעֵ֣י יָדָ֑יו מִידֵי֙ אֲבִ֣יר יַעֲקֹ֔ב מִשָּׁ֥ם רֹעֶ֖ה אֶ֥בֶן יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: But remained in steadiness his bow, and were agile [the] arms of his hands, from [the] hands of [the] Mighty One of Jacob; from there [the] Shepherd, [the] Stone of Israel,
pieces: Yet his bow did not waver, and his arms were kept nimble by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob; from there, from the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel,

L.24: But his bow remained steady, and the arms of his hands were made agile by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, from there, the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel,

R.24: But Joseph held his bow steady, and his arms stayed strong. The Mighty One of Jacob gave him strength. That help came from the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel.

decisions.choice: the Mighty One of Jacob: a title of God
decisions.reason: Avir, "mighty one", is used of God in this phrase here and in Psalm 132:2, 5 and Isaiah 49:26; 60:16. Jacob had called God "the Fear of Isaac" (31:42); here he names him from his own experience.

decisions.choice: from there, the Shepherd
alternatives: by the name of the Shepherd
from there he became the shepherd
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels read "from there": Joseph's help came from the place of the Mighty One, from the Shepherd. The same letters with other vowels mean "from the name", "by the name of the Shepherd", as the Syriac and the Aramaic translations read it. Some take the line to say that from there Joseph became a shepherd. The meaning of the line is uncertain; the Hebrew vowels are followed here.

decisions.choice: the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel
decisions.reason: Jacob called God his shepherd when he blessed Joseph's sons (48:15). "Stone of Israel" is found only here; it may recall the stone Jacob set up at Bethel (28:18-22). God is the firm foundation of his people, as he is called the Rock in Deuteronomy 32:4.

decisions.choice: his bow remained steady: he held firm
decisions.reason: Under attack, Joseph did not give way, because God's hands strengthened his own.

decisions.choice: The Mighty One of Jacob gave him strength
alternatives: from the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what the hands of God did for Joseph.

records.source: מֵאֵ֨ל אָבִ֜יךָ וְיַעְזְרֶ֗ךָּ וְאֵ֤ת שַׁדַּי֙ וִיבָ֣רְכֶ֔ךָּ בִּרְכֹ֤ת שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ מֵעָ֔ל בִּרְכֹ֥ת תְּה֖וֹם רֹבֶ֣צֶת תָּ֑חַת בִּרְכֹ֥ת שָׁדַ֖יִם וָרָֽחַם׃
records.gloss: from [the] God of your father, and he will help you, and with [the] Almighty, and he will bless you, blessings of heaven from above, blessings of [the] deep lying beneath, blessings of breasts and womb.
pieces: from the God of your father, who will help you, and by the Almighty, who will bless you with blessings that fall from the sky above, blessings that rise from the deep lying below, blessings of breast and womb.

L.25: from the God of your father, who will help you, and by the Almighty, who will bless you with blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lies beneath, blessings of breasts and womb.

R.25: Your father's God will help you. God Almighty will bless you. He will send rain from the sky above and water from deep under the ground. He will give you many children and many young animals.

decisions.choice: and by the Almighty
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "and with Shaddai". Some Hebrew manuscripts, the Samaritan Pentateuch, and the Greek and Syriac translations read "and El Shaddai", God Almighty, which differs by one letter. The meaning is the same; the Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: Shaddai ... breasts: a play on sound
decisions.reason: Shaddai, the Almighty, sounds like shadayim, "breasts". The God who is named Shaddai gives the blessing of children.

decisions.choice: heaven, the deep, breasts and womb: every source of life
decisions.reason: Rain from the sky, springs from the waters below the earth (7:11), and the birth of children and young animals: the blessing covers all that makes a family and its flocks thrive.

decisions.choice: lies: crouches
decisions.reason: The verb is used of an animal lying down, as of Issachar's donkey (verse 14). The deep waters lie beneath the earth like a beast at rest.

decisions.choice: rain ... water ... many children and many young animals
alternatives: blessings of heaven, the deep, breasts and womb
decisions.reason: Readable explains what each blessing means (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: who will help you, who will bless you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the verbs with "and"; English says it with "who", which needs no pronoun for God.

records.source: בִּרְכֹ֣ת אָבִ֗יךָ גָּֽבְרוּ֙ עַל־בִּרְכֹ֣ת הוֹרַ֔י עַֽד־תַּאֲוַ֖ת גִּבְעֹ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם תִּֽהְיֶ֨ין֙לְרֹ֣אשׁ יוֹסֵ֔ף וּלְקָדְקֹ֖ד נְזִ֥יר אֶחָֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: [The] blessings of your father have prevailed over [the] blessings of my progenitors, to [the] boundary of [the] everlasting hills; may they be on [the] head of Joseph, and on [the] crown of [the] head of [the] one set apart [among] his brothers.
pieces: The blessings your father gives are stronger than the blessings of my forebears, as far as the farthest of the ancient hills. Let them come down on Joseph's head, on the crown of the one marked out from his brothers.

L.26: The blessings of your father are mightier than the blessings of my forefathers, up to the bounds of the everlasting hills. May they be on the head of Joseph, and on the crown of the head of the one set apart from his brothers.

R.26: The blessings I am giving you are greater than the blessings my own fathers received. They reach as far as the oldest hills. May all these blessings come down on Joseph, the son who was separated from his brothers.

decisions.choice: the blessings of my forefathers, up to the bounds of the everlasting hills
alternatives: the blessings of the ancient mountains, the bounty of the everlasting hills
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels read "those who conceived me, up to", that is Jacob's fathers Abraham and Isaac. The same letters, divided and voweled differently, read "the ancient mountains", which gives a neat parallel with "the everlasting hills" and matches Moses' blessing of Joseph (Deuteronomy 33:15) and the Greek translation. The word taavah can mean "boundary" or "desire, delight". The Hebrew vowels are followed here, but the other reading is well supported.

decisions.choice: the one set apart: nazir
decisions.reason: Nazir means one separated or consecrated, the word later used of Nazirites (Numbers 6:2). It is related to nezer, "crown", so it can also mean the one crowned among his brothers. Joseph was separated from his brothers when they sold him and was raised to rule over them. Deuteronomy 33:16 repeats the line.

decisions.choice: your father: Jacob speaking of himself
decisions.reason: Jacob speaks of himself in the third person, as a father blessing his son.

decisions.choice: The blessings I am giving you
decisions.reason: Readable puts Jacob's words about himself in the first person (meaning decision m3).

records.source: בִּנְיָמִין֙ זְאֵ֣ב יִטְרָ֔ף בַּבֹּ֖קֶר יֹ֣אכַל עַ֑ד וְלָעֶ֖רֶב יְחַלֵּ֥ק שָׁלָֽל׃
records.gloss: Benjamin [is] a wolf [that] tears; in the morning he eats [the] prey, and at evening he divides [the] spoil.
pieces: Benjamin is a wolf that tears its prey: in the morning he feeds on the kill, by evening he is sharing out the spoils."

L.27: Benjamin is a wolf that tears; in the morning he devours the prey, and in the evening he divides the spoil."

R.27: Benjamin is like a hungry wolf. In the morning he eats what he has caught. In the evening he shares out what he has taken."

decisions.choice: Benjamin the wolf: fierce in war
decisions.reason: The tribe of Benjamin was known for its fighters (Judges 3:15; 20:15-16), and Israel's first king, Saul, came from it (1 Samuel 9:1-2).

decisions.choice: morning ... evening: all day long
decisions.reason: From morning to evening the wolf is busy with its prey: Benjamin will never lack spoil.

records.source: כָּל־אֵ֛לֶּה שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֑ר וְ֠זֹאת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֨ר לָהֶ֤ם אֲבִיהֶם֙ וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אוֹתָ֔ם אִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר כְּבִרְכָת֖וֹ בֵּרַ֥ךְ אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: All these [are the] tribes of Israel, twelve, and this [is] what spoke to them their father, and he blessed them; each according to his blessing he blessed them.
pieces: Together these make up the twelve tribes of Israel. These are the words their father spoke over them when he blessed them; to each he gave a blessing of his own.

L.28: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father spoke to them when he blessed them; he blessed each one with his own blessing.

R.28: These twelve sons became the twelve tribes of Israel. Their father blessed each one of them, and these were his words. Each son received his own blessing.

decisions.choice: the twelve tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: The first time the Bible speaks of the twelve tribes: the twelve sons of one man have become the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: each with his own blessing
decisions.reason: Not every saying was a blessing in the usual sense: Reuben, Simeon and Levi heard rebukes. Each son received the word that fitted him.

decisions.choice: These twelve sons became
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the sons stand for the tribes descended from them.

records.source: וַיְצַ֣ו אוֹתָ֗ם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אֲנִי֙ נֶאֱסָ֣ף אֶל־עַמִּ֔י קִבְר֥וּ אֹתִ֖י אֶל־אֲבֹתָ֑י אֶל־הַ֨מְּעָרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּשְׂדֵ֖ה עֶפְר֥וֹן הַֽחִתִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And he commanded them and said to them, I [am] about to be gathered to my people; bury me with my fathers in the cave that [is] in [the] field of Ephron the Hittite,
pieces: Then he charged them: "I am soon to be gathered to my people. Lay me to rest with my fathers in the cave that lies in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

L.29: And he commanded them and said to them, "I am about to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

R.29: Then Jacob told his sons what they must do: "I am about to die and join my family who have died before me. Bury me where my ancestors are buried, in the cave in the field that Ephron the Hittite once owned.

decisions.choice: gathered to my people: to die and join one's ancestors
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of Abraham (25:8), Ishmael (25:17) and Isaac (35:29). It speaks of joining those who have died before, not only of burial.

decisions.choice: the cave of Ephron the Hittite
decisions.reason: Abraham bought this field and cave to bury Sarah (chapter 23): the only land the family owned in Canaan.

decisions.choice: die and join my family who have died before me
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.

records.source: בַּמְּעָרָ֞ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר בִּשְׂדֵ֧ה הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֛ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־פְּנֵי־מַמְרֵ֖א בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן אֲשֶׁר֩ קָנָ֨ה אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה מֵאֵ֛ת עֶפְרֹ֥ן הַחִתִּ֖י לַאֲחֻזַּת־קָֽבֶר׃
records.gloss: in the cave that [is] in [the] field of Machpelah, which [is] before Mamre, in [the] land of Canaan, which bought Abraham with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a possession of a burial place.
pieces: the cave in the Machpelah field, east of Mamre in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought, field and all, from Ephron the Hittite to own as a burial site.

L.30: in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought along with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a burial possession.

R.30: That field is called Machpelah, and it lies near Mamre in the land of Canaan. Abraham bought the field from Ephron the Hittite so his family would have their own place to bury their dead.

decisions.choice: before Mamre: east of Mamre
decisions.reason: "Before" or "facing" can mean east, the direction a person faced when giving directions (23:17, 19).

decisions.choice: a burial possession: land owned outright
decisions.reason: Jacob stresses the purchase: the cave belonged to the family by right, a first holding in the promised land.

records.source: שָׁ֣מָּה קָֽבְר֞וּ אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֗ם וְאֵת֙ שָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ שָׁ֚מָּה קָבְר֣וּ אֶת־יִצְחָ֔ק וְאֵ֖ת רִבְקָ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְשָׁ֥מָּה קָבַ֖רְתִּי אֶת־לֵאָֽה׃
records.gloss: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.
pieces: That is where Abraham was laid to rest with his wife Sarah, and Isaac with his wife Rebekah; and I laid Leah there too.

L.31: There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.

R.31: Abraham and Sarah his wife were buried in that cave. So were Isaac and his wife Rebekah. I put Leah's body there too.

decisions.choice: Leah: buried with the patriarchs
decisions.reason: Genesis does not tell of Leah's death or of Rebekah's burial; we learn of them only here. Rachel, the wife Jacob loved, lies by the road to Bethlehem (48:7), but Jacob will lie beside Leah, the mother of Judah and Levi.

decisions.choice: they buried: people buried
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; Abraham was buried by Isaac and Ishmael (25:9), Isaac by Esau and Jacob (35:29).

records.source: מִקְנֵ֧ה הַשָּׂדֶ֛ה וְהַמְּעָרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־בּ֖וֹ מֵאֵ֥ת בְּנֵי־חֵֽת׃
records.gloss: [The] purchase of the field and the cave that [is] in it [was] from [the] sons of Heth.
pieces: The field with its cave was a purchase from the Hittites."

L.32: The field and the cave that is in it were purchased from the sons of Heth."

R.32: Abraham bought the field and its cave from the Hittites."

decisions.choice: purchase: something acquired
decisions.reason: Miqneh usually means livestock, a man's wealth, but here, as in 23:18, it is a property bought.

decisions.choice: the Hittites
decisions.reason: "Sons of Heth" means the Hittites (23:3, 10).

records.source: וַיְכַ֤ל יַעֲקֹב֙ לְצַוֺּ֣ת אֶת־בָּנָ֔יו וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף רַגְלָ֖יו אֶל־הַמִּטָּ֑ה וַיִּגְוַ֖ע וַיֵּאָ֥סֶף אֶל־עַמָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And finished Jacob commanding his sons, and he gathered his feet into the bed, and he expired, and he was gathered to his peoples.
pieces: Jacob finished charging his sons. Then he lifted his feet back onto the bed, took his last breath, and was gathered to his people.

L.33: And when Jacob finished commanding his sons, he drew his feet into the bed, and breathed his last, and was gathered to his people.

R.33: Jacob finished giving his sons their orders. Then he pulled his feet up onto his bed. He took one last breath and died, and he joined his ancestors.

decisions.choice: drew his feet into the bed
decisions.reason: Jacob had sat up on the edge of the bed to bless his sons (48:2). Now he lies back down and dies.

decisions.choice: gathered to his people: joined his ancestors in death
decisions.reason: He is "gathered to his people" at the moment of death, though he will not be buried for months (chapter 50): the phrase speaks of more than a grave.

decisions.choice: he joined his ancestors
alternatives: he was gathered to his people
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom.
